entities.name: Servius Sulpicius Rufus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Servius Sulpicius Rufus was a Roman orator and jurist who played a pivotal role in shaping the country's political landscape. As consul in 51 BC, he worked to establish a more stable government.

Born into a prominent family, Servius Sulpicius Rufus was educated at the best schools in Rome. His natural talent for rhetoric and law earned him recognition from the Roman elite.

Rufus's most significant achievement came when he helped pass the Lex Julia, a landmark legislation that reformed the Roman calendar. This move not only improved the accuracy of timekeeping but also had far-reaching implications for trade, commerce, and military operations.

Despite his many accomplishments, Rufus's legacy was somewhat overshadowed by his later life as a client of Julius Caesar. However, his work on the Lex Julia remains an important milestone in Roman history, demonstrating the power of effective governance and legislation.

Servius Sulpicius Rufus may not have been a household name during his lifetime, but his impact on Rome's development continues to be felt today.
